title: Dock Drift
summary: Guide a robot drifting off a space-station rail into its docking clamp, using logarithmic differentiation to find the slope.
subject: mathematics
concepts: Logarithmic differentiation of products and quotients
Derivative of u(x)^v(x) by taking logs
Roots of quotients by taking logs
Differentiate a sum term by term
Simplifying by a trigonometric substitution first
learningOutcome: The student can differentiate products, quotients, roots and powers like u(x)^v(x) by taking logs, and inverse trigonometric functions after a substitution, then evaluate the slope at a point.

levels.title: Many factors
levels.adds: Baseline: for a product or quotient take logs, so y′/y is a sum of terms like m/(x − a); multiply by y at the point (Ex 5.5 Q1, Q16, Q17).
hints: log y turns the product into a sum: log y = m log|x − a| + n log|x − b|.
Differentiate: y′/y = m/(x − a) + n/(x − b), and a factor in the denominator gives a minus sign.
Find y at the release point, multiply, then times the distance to the wall.

levels.title: Power towers
levels.adds: New: y = u^v. Take logs, log y = v log u, so y′/y = v′ log u + v u′/u; when u = 1 the log term vanishes (Ex 5.5 Q3, Q4, Q7).
hints: Neither the power rule nor the exponential rule works when both base and exponent vary.
log y = v log u, so y′ = y(v′ log u + v u′/u).
At the release point the base is 1, so log u = 0 and y = 1.

levels.title: Root rails
levels.adds: Harder: a square root of a quotient. log y = ½[log|x − a| + log|x − b| − log|x − c| …] (Ex 5.5 Q2).
hints: Take logs first: the root becomes a factor ½ in front of the sum.
Each factor under the root gives ±1/(x − r) inside the bracket.
Work out y itself at the point: it is a whole number here.

levels.title: Sums of towers
levels.adds: New: for a sum such as x^x + (2x − 1)^x, differentiate each term on its own; log of a sum does not split (Ex 5.5 Q5 to Q11).
hints: Write y = u + v and find u′ and v′ separately.
Take logs of each term, never of the whole sum.
Add the two slopes at the release point.

levels.title: Inverse trig rails
levels.adds: New: derivatives of sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹ and tan⁻¹; substitute x = tan θ or sin θ to simplify first (Ex 5.3 Q9 to Q15).
hints: With x = tan θ, 2x/(1 + x²) = sin 2θ, so sin⁻¹(2x/(1 + x²)) = 2 tan⁻¹ x here.
Check the range of x: it decides which simplification is true.

misconceptions: The derivative of x^x is x·x^(x − 1)
log(u + v) = log u + log v
sin⁻¹(2x/(1 + x²)) is always 2 tan⁻¹ x
